title: Why are people saying Julia Stiles went to Juilliard? The DWTS joke
answer: It's a joke about her movie role, not her real life. In "Save the Last Dance" (2001), Julia Stiles played a ballet dancer who auditions for Juilliard. When she joined "Dancing With the Stars" in 2026, fans joked she had an unfair advantage because she "went to Juilliard." She never attended or auditioned there.
body:
When people say Julia Stiles "went to Juilliard," they are blurring the actress with Sara, the character she played in "Save the Last Dance," the 2001 hit about a teenage ballet dancer whose big goal is a Juilliard audition. It is the kind of line that shows up under a dance clip: "Not fair, she literally trained at Juilliard," usually followed by a laughing emoji.

The joke took off on Sept. 2, 2026, when Stiles was announced as part of the cast of "Dancing With the Stars" Season 35, paired with pro Ezra Sosa. Sosa posted a TikTok captioned "last dance? not even close," and commenters quickly called it "cheating" because of her supposed Juilliard training. Juilliard itself weighed in on Instagram, confirming she was never a student there, which Sosa jokingly called "a bit shady."

Stiles set the record straight herself. She told E! News she never attended or even auditioned for Juilliard, and she told Us Weekly she is "not a professional dancer" and had "just played pretend" in the film. In real life she studied at Columbia University. She leaned into the nostalgia anyway: in Week 5 of the show she re-created her character's famous audition scene.

Stiles and Sosa were eliminated on Nov. 2, 2026, on the show's Disney on Broadway night, ahead of the quarterfinals. The Juilliard line keeps resurfacing as clips from her run circulate while Season 35 heads to its finale, and newer viewers who missed September's back-and-forth are asking where it came from.
in_the_news: Searches for the Juilliard joke picked up again in mid-November 2026 as "Dancing With the Stars" Season 35 neared its finale.
